A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same framework paper. Their complete text, Figure 1, Table 1, and references are readable and support reliable comparison. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: Section 3.1 reports the authors' keyword analysis of 4,140 ACL papers and category percentages. Section 5.1 reports original mapping of approximately 20 examples from each of five stereotype resources, illustrated in Table 1.

after.justification: v2 retains the original ACL-paper analysis in Section 3.1 and the dataset-mapping exercise and findings in Section 5.1 and Table 1.

M1.justification: The five-component framework—target group, attribute, association, perceiver, and context—and its implementation recommendations remain unchanged. Added references do not introduce a new method component.

E1.justification: Both versions analyze the same ACL literature coverage and map examples from SeeGULL, StereoLMs, SPICE, CrowsPairs, and Social Bias Frames. No additional dataset, population, modality, or task is actually investigated.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates competing methods against the proposed framework. Table 1 contains the same five source resources; the newly cited studies are not evaluated as baselines.

E3.justification: The reported keyword-query approach and mapping of approximately 20 examples per dataset are unchanged. No new evaluation procedure, metric, sample size, or experimental setting is introduced.

E4.justification: Section 5.1 retains the same illustrative mapping and observations about inapplicable warmth/competence categories and missing perceiver information. No new case study, ablation, sensitivity analysis, or robustness test appears.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated runs, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or other uncertainty-estimation procedures for its original analyses.

E6.justification: The ACL analysis remains at 4,140 papers, with 54.1% mentioning gender stereotypes, 25.8% racial stereotypes, and 16.4% region/nationality stereotypes. All Table 1 entries and dataset-mapping findings are unchanged.

T1.justification: Neither version presents mathematical definitions, theorems, or proofs. The added description of prior work on stereotype dimensions is conceptual background, not a formal theoretical development.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and closing Discussion retain the same contribution: a unified five-component framework for operationalizing stereotypes, accompanied by implementation and responsible-use recommendations.

C2.justification: The interpretations of dataset gaps, proposed applications, and Section 7 limitations are unchanged. Replacing 'prioritize stereotypes' with 'prioritize debiasing efforts' clarifies an existing recommendation without changing its substance.

D1.justification: The mapping description and recommendations concerning spreadsheets, relational databases, and knowledge graphs are retained. No implementation settings, reproducibility instructions, or code/data access information are added or revised.

R1.justification: v2 adds Nicolas et al. (2021, 2022) and Nicolas and Caliskan (2024a,b). Sections 2, 3.2, and 4 briefly acknowledge additional stereotype dimensions, applications to LLMs, and support for attribute characterization, modestly expanding the related-work context.

P1.justification: v2 adds brief background passages, refines the valence recommendation, and corrects the swapped email addresses of the first two authors. The section hierarchy and almost all prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 1 and Table 1 retain identical content and presentation. Text and references reflow across pages, and v2 leaves substantial blank space below the Discussion continuation in page 9's left column. These are limited layout changes.

improvement.justification: The added discussion of previously unmentioned stereotype-content research modestly improves scholarly grounding at the paper's central psychology/NLP intersection. The debiasing wording and author-contact corrections also improve clarity and accuracy. The framework and original evidence remain unchanged, limiting the gain; page 9's added whitespace is a small presentation drawback.
